thread.title: Here are the 13 most useful Mac shortcuts that will help you do everything faster (AAPL)

author: Sean Wolfe
title: Here are the 13 most useful Mac shortcuts that will help you do everything faster (AAPL)
text: Selecting everything, especially in a big document, can take ages. Hitting ⌘ + A selects everything instantly. 4 / 4) ⌘ + C / ⌘ + V — Copy or paste Max Slater-Robins / BI Copying and pasting text with the Mac trackpad can be a struggle, but typing ⌘ + C (which copies) and then ⌘ + V (which pastes) makes it much easier. This shortcut works with text, photos, and anything else that can be copied. 5 / 5) ⌘ + W — Close an app window Max Slater-Robins / BI Locating the small red circle to close app windows quickly can be tricky. Use ⌘ + W to close windows easily. 6 / 6) ⌘ + ⌥ + Esc — Force quit apps Max Slater-Robins / BI Having apps crash is annoying and the quick way to fix the problem is to press ⌘ + ⌥ + Esc. This opens up a menu, showing all running apps with any that are not working marked with "Not Responding." 7 / 7) ⌘ + Tab — Switch apps Max Slater-Robins / BI Using the dock to switch apps is okay, but switching them by pressing ⌘ + Tab is quicker. All of your apps are displayed in a row and can be accessed by pressing tab again or clicking on the one you want. 8 / 8) ⌘ + ↑ / ⌘ + ↓ — Scroll up or down a page Max Slater-Robins / BI Scrolling up or down a page can take a while. To instantly scroll to the top, press ⌘ + ↑ — and for the bottom, press ⌘ + ↓. 9 / 9) ⌃ + Tab — Change tabs in Chrome or Safari Max Slater-Robins / BI Press ⌃ (Control) + Tab to smoothly change tabs in Safari, Chrome, and other browsers. You can also press ⌃ (Control) + Shift + Tab to change tabs in the other direction. 10 / 10) ⌘ + ~ — Quickly change app windows Max Slater-Robins / BI If you need to have a lot of windows for one app open, then ⌘ + ~ will be a godsend. It switches between different windows of the same app — if you have two different Pages documents open, for example. 11 / 11) ⌘ + , — Open app preferences Max Slater-Robins / BI App preferences are hidden behind the  and another button, but pressing ⌘ + , (comma) brings them to the front for whichever app is open. 12 / 12) ⌘ + H — Hide the app Max Slater-Robins / BI You can minimise apps in OS X using ⌘ + M. But if you'd rather hide the app altogether, then hit ⌘ + H and it'll instantly vanish. 13 /
